headline: Seasonal Access and Wilderness Permits
reservation: Everglades National Park does not currently require a timed-entry permit for general vehicle access, but boat tours from Flamingo and Gulf Coast should be reserved well in advance. Backcountry camping requires a specific permit obtained through the official wilderness system. Always check the official NPS site for current water levels and facility closures before traveling.

days.title: Wetlands and Wildlife Observation

stops.name: Anhinga Trail
stops.detail: Walk the boardwalk to spot alligators, turtles, and diverse wading birds in the sawgrass marsh.

stops.name: Pa-hay-okee Overlook
stops.detail: Ascend the observation platform for a panoramic view of the 'River of Grass' ecosystem.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for park road transit; conditions vary
days.note: Winter months offer the best wildlife visibility as water levels drop and animals congregate.

days.title: Coastal Mangroves and Florida Bay

stops.name: Mahogany Hammock
stops.detail: Explore a 'tree island' featuring the largest living mahogany trees in the United States.

stops.name: Flamingo Marina
stops.detail: View the transition to saltwater habitats and look for manatees and crocodiles in the basin.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for return drive to Homestead; conditions vary
days.note: Insect activity is extremely high in mangrove areas; prepare accordingly with physical barriers.

days.title: The Northern Corridor and Sawgrass Marshes

stops.name: Shark Valley Tram Road
stops.detail: Explore the 15-mile loop via bicycle or guided tram to reach the 65-foot observation tower.

stops.name: Miccosukee Cultural Area
stops.detail: Learn about the indigenous history and contemporary relationship with the Everglades landscape.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour from Miami/Homestead to Shark Valley; conditions vary
days.note: Shark Valley is a separate entrance from the main park road; allow ample travel time between them.

intel.title: Shark Valley Limits
intel.text: The parking lot at Shark Valley is small and frequently fills by mid-morning during the dry season. Arrive early or expect a one-in, one-out wait at the gated entrance.

intel.title: Remote Interior
intel.text: Cellular service is non-existent throughout most of the main park road and the Flamingo area. Use the Ernest F. Coe Visitor Center for final digital communications before heading south.

intel.title: Last Chance Supplies
intel.text: Homestead is the primary location for fuel and groceries before entering the southern park gate. Limited fuel may be available at Flamingo, but availability is not guaranteed.

intel.title: Mosquito Season
intel.text: During the summer wet season, mosquito populations can be hazardous in shaded hammock and mangrove trails. Dry season (December–April) is the preferred window for land-based exploration.

intel.title: Waterway Navigation
intel.text: Paddling routes and boat launches are subject to tidal changes and seasonal water levels. Check with a ranger at the Gulf Coast or Flamingo stations for current hazards.

plan.arrival: First two hours: Pickup rental at MIA, stock up on water and sun protection in Homestead, and stop at Ernest F. Coe Visitor Center.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are suitable for the main paved roads; RVs should check height clearances for specific hammock boardwalk areas.
plan.goldenHour: The Pa-hay-okee Overlook provides an unobstructed 360-degree view for sunset, though park exit times must be observed.
